cards.front: Recall a key point about Tort Law & Negligence
cards.back: A tort is a civil wrong — the claimant sues the defendant for compensation, unlike criminal law where the state prosecutes

cards.front: Recall a key point about Tort Law & Negligence
cards.back: Negligence is the most common tort — it requires duty of care, breach of that duty, causation and resulting damage

cards.front: Recall a key point about Tort Law & Negligence
cards.back: Duty of care exists where the defendant owed a legal duty to the claimant — established by the Caparo three-stage test

cards.front: Recall a key point about Tort Law & Negligence
cards.back: The Caparo test requires: (1) foreseeability of harm, (2) proximity of relationship and (3) it is fair, just and reasonable to impose a duty

cards.front: Recall a key point about Tort Law & Negligence
cards.back: Breach of duty occurs where the defendant fell below the standard of the reasonable person — the objective test

cards.front: Recall a key point about Tort Law & Negligence
cards.back: The reasonable person takes reasonable precautions against foreseeable risks — professionals must meet the standard of their profession

cards.front: Recall a key point about Tort Law & Negligence
cards.back: Causation requires both factual causation ('but for' the defendant's negligence, would the harm have occurred?) and legal causation (was the negligence the proximate cause?)

cards.front: Recall a key point about Tort Law & Negligence
cards.back: Damage must be reasonably foreseeable and not too remote — the defendant is only liable for damage that is a foreseeable consequence of the breach

cards.front: Recall a key point about Tort Law & Negligence
cards.back: Contributory negligence reduces the claimant's damages if they were partly at fault for their own injury — damages are reduced proportionally

cards.front: Recall a key point about Tort Law & Negligence
cards.back: Vicarious liability means an employer can be held liable for the torts of employees committed in the course of employment

cards.front: Recall a key point about Tort Law & Negligence
cards.back: Remedies in tort are mainly damages (compensation) but injunctions are available to prevent ongoing harm

cards.front: Recall a key point about Tort Law & Negligence
cards.back: The tort of negligence has expanded significantly since Donoghue v Stevenson (1932) but courts have recently limited its scope

cards.front: What should you know about gcse law exam tips — tort law & negligence?
cards.back: 1. For Tort Law & Negligence questions, identify the relevant area of law and state the legal principles clearly 2. Apply legal rules to the facts of the scenario — don't just state the law 3. When evaluating, consider both the effectiveness and fairness of legal rules 4. Reference relevant cases and statutes when discussing Tort Law & Negligence 5. Consider reform proposals and alternative approaches where relevant
